verdict.rationale: Alacritty's configuration is a plain-text TOML file covering fonts, colors, window, scrollback, environment and keybindings, which can be versioned in dotfiles. It also supports importing additional config files and skips missing ones, which allows a shared base config plus per-machine overrides. Missing for 10: documented config file locations/search paths for portable dotfile placement, explicit first-party guidance on syncing across machines, independent hands-on corroboration of a dotfiles workflow (one user reports config gotchas after the switch to TOML).

support.subject: As a power-user, I can keep the terminal's full configuration as plain-text files in my dotfiles and sync it across machines

citations.quote: Alacritty's configuration file uses the TOML format.
Imports are loaded in order, skipping all missing files, with the importing file being loaded last.
Alacritty is a modern terminal emulator that comes with sensible defaults, but allows for extensive configuration.
